name: gizza-ai/image-average-color
summary: Compute the single mean color of an image (with a gamma-correct variant)

tool.description: Compute the single average (mean) color of an image. Returns two means: 'simple', the naive per-channel arithmetic mean of the sRGB values (what most average-color tools report), and 'gamma_correct', the perceptually correct mean taken in linear light (sRGB decoded to linear, averaged, then re-encoded) — the recommended value. Each mean is given as #rrggbb hex, #rrggbbaa hex, rgb()/rgba()/hsl() strings, the r/g/b/a channels (0-255) and h/s/l values. Also returns the image dimensions, how many pixels were counted, the perceived brightness (0-100) and an is_dark flag for the gamma-correct mean (use white text on a dark mean), and its complementary hex color. By default (near-)transparent pixels are ignored; set ignore_transparency=false to fold every pixel in. Provide the image as either url (HTTP/HTTPS) or ref (id from a prior tool call).

url.description: Image URL (HTTP/HTTPS). Use either url or ref.

ref.description: Reference id from a prior tool call. Use either url or ref.

ignore_transparency.description: Exclude (near-)transparent pixels from the average so a transparent PNG background doesn't drag the mean toward black. Optional — defaults to true; set false to fold every pixel in.
